correctness.rationale: CDF inversion and the chain rule give Q_a'(u)=1/[a u B((-log u)/a)]. For z=e^(-w), z<−log(1−z)<z/(1−z) gives B'>0 and B''<0. With B(0+)=0, strict concavity and monotonicity give ρB(w)<B(ρw)<B(w) for ρ=r/s. Integration against Q_r' gives both strict interval bounds. B(w) tends to 1 at infinity and is asymptotic to w log(1/w) at zero, so the derivative ratio tends to ρ and 1 at the two ends, respectively. Its positive weighted averages over shrinking near-endpoint intervals approach the same limits. Both transport constants follow since both quantiles span R. The centered successive quantile differences are strictly increasing and integrable with mean zero, so their proper initial integrals are negative; the equal-mean integrated-quantile criterion gives both convex comparisons. The two logarithmic tails justify integrability. The representative ratio at (1,2,0.2,0.8) was independently evaluated as 0.674717885639053; only the analytic check supports the continuum claim.
residual_risks: Numerics corroborate one example and are not required for sharpness or any universal quantifier.
